title: introduce-session-sliced-cost-attribution-and-span-join-visualizer
author: Priya Menon
description: Context and motivation: Production teams need faster root-cause for cost spikes that happen inside long-running chat sessions and better visual tools to reconcile traces with cost signals. Existing token-level and span telemetry gives good signal but is hard to correlate at the session/fragments level for ops and product teams. This PR introduces two complementary features: 1) session-sliced cost attribution — a backend aggregation and set of derived metrics that break down per-session cost and latency into contiguous 'slices' (prompt fragments, model-variant boundaries, KV-cache resets) so you can answer questions like 'which fragment of this session consumed 60% of the cost' quickly; 2) span-join visualizer — a console widget that joins contiguous spans and log events into a compact timeline view with cost/latency overlays and clickable links back to traces and the new session slices. Summary of changes: - New aggregator service: observability/session_slicer service (Go) that consumes traces + token cost events and emits slice-level rollups (rw_session_slice_* metrics) and a lightweight JSON join artifact stored in S3 for UI retrieval. - Tracing pipeline change: tracing/span_joiner processor (Python) that synthesizes contiguous span groups and enriches them with the slice id from the session_slicer. - Console: dashboards/session-cost-explorer and console widget span-join-visualizer (React/TS) with timeline, per-slice cost bars, and a filter for model-variant and cache-hit state. - Alerts: a new adaptive alert rule (observability/alerts/session_slice_burn_rate.prom) that compares slice burn-rate to a session baseline and suppresses noisy transient spikes by requiring multi-slice persistence. - SDK & ingestion: small opt-in telemetry flag in runtime to emit per-slice annotations for high-cardinality sessions to reduce downstream join load. - Tests: unit and integration tests for the pipeline, e2e storybook for the UI widget, and a load test harness demonstrating slice throughput at 10k sessions/minute. Migration and rollout: The session_slicer initially runs on a dedicated observability queue (no replacement of existing token rollups). We will run the slicer in shadow mode for 2 weeks and run a limited console beta. Rollout steps: 1) Deploy backend in shadow mode -> 2) Enable UI for beta orgs (feature flag) -> 3) Flip ingestion opt-in for consenting customers -> 4) Promote to default. Why this is different: instead of trying to attribute cost purely to tokens or spans, slices represent contiguous logical units inside a session (prompt, tool-call, external context), which is more actionable for product owners. The span-join visualizer is designed to be low-cardinality and link back to full traces when operators need detail. Testing notes: - Local unit tests and integration tests in ./tracing/span_joiner/tests pass. - Load test harness (observability/loadtests/session_slicer/) simulates 10k sessions/min and shows CPU/latency within expected SLOs (cluster sizing notes in runbook). - CI initially failed lint due to TS type and a flake8 rule; both were fixed in subsequent commits. Observability & cost: new metrics introduced: rw_session_slice_count, rw_session_slice_token_cost_total, rw_session_slice_latency_ms_p50/p95, rw_span_join_count. These metrics are emitted with low-cardinality tags (slice_type, model_family, region) and a session_bucket id that reuses existing sampling keys to avoid explosion. Rollback plan: disable feature flag and stop emitting slice artifacts; slice rollups are additive and do not replace existing billing signals. Related: ENG-1284 (slo-driven alert tuning), PM-482 (console explorer for billing teams). Checklist: - [x] Backend aggregator implemented - [x] Tracing joiner implemented - [x] Console widget + dashboard - [x] Tests and load harness - [x] Runbook and rollout flag - [x] Docs (observability/docs/session-slices.md)

review_comments: Samir Patel: This looks great overall. Two questions: how are we preventing cardinality explosion for multi-tenant customers that have long-lived sessions? Can you add documentation on how session_bucket works?

Priya Menon (author): We already reuse the existing sampling key (session_bucket) and explicitly drop per-token annotations unless the session is opted-in. Added docs at observability/docs/session-slices.md describing the bucketing and sampling policy.

Claire Huang: The alert suppression rule seems complex. Can we simplify the logic so on-call can reason about it quickly? Maybe prefer a refractory window rather than a multi-slice persistence counter?

Priya Menon: Happy to iterate. We started with refractory windows but observed oscillation in canary tests. The multi-slice persistence gate reduces noise from short-lived tool calls. Added comments and a README explaining tradeoffs.
Daniel Reilly: UI looks solid. A couple of accessibility items and keyboard nav for the timeline would be nice. Also consider linking directly to the trace span id when available.
Priya Menon: Addressed keyboard nav (tab focus) and added deep-links to trace/span ids where present.
release_notes: Add session-sliced cost attribution and span-join visualizer: new low-cardinality metrics and console widget for per-session cost/latency breakdowns. Beta rollout behind feature flag. See observability/docs/session-slices.md for details.
